case_result.must_exhaust: The sole local-alliance piece, in full, moved to the bottom half of its Army box.
case_result.consequences: Remove all unrest in attacked region; associated Commander takes a trophy, subject to p33 vacant-Commander exception if applicable.

counting_rule.preferred_application: The specific p33 instruction counts newly exhausted physical Army pieces, including an eligible local-alliance piece; one physical alliance is one such piece.
counting_rule.qualification: p22 broadly says alliance strength can defend. It does not provide an explicit defense conversion formula. A weighted-strength interpretation is consequently a real competing whole-text inference, not an express p33 statement.

no_splitting.interpretive_limit: The sentence about purposes explicitly prohibits splitting between purposes; the independent each-piece-once sentence prevents reuse even within the same type of purpose. Neither sentence says a piece may be used only when its printed number exactly matches the opposing strength.

crisis_2_same_single_alliance.preferred_literal_p33_result: Exhaust the sole piece as many as possible; only one newly exhausted physical piece against strength 2, so Crisis succeeds and defense fails.
crisis_2_same_single_alliance.weighted_alternative: If p22 is read as importing the printed strength into defense, this alliance supplies defense 2 and holds against Crisis 2.

more_active_pieces_than_crisis_strength.result: Exhaust the required number of physical pieces, not every active piece.
more_active_pieces_than_crisis_strength.basis: p33 equal to the strength ... or as many as possible; the latter applies when there are too few.

printed_alliance_strength_exceeds_crisis.stated_case: No obstacle: the physical piece count is exactly 1. Full exhaustion does not split strength across purposes.
printed_alliance_strength_exceeds_crisis.player_aid_support: The Crisis table says defender wins ties and describes the defender by exhausted units, which supports ordinary defense meeting or exceeding attack. It does not supply an explicit alliance weighting formula or exhaust-selection procedure for weighted overshoot.

remaining_precise_uncertainty.issue: For other cases in which physical-piece count and summed printed alliance strength produce different outcomes, p22 general strength language and p33 specific piece-count language leave a competing weighted reading. I prefer literal p33 piece count but do not claim the supplied sources expressly settle intended numerical alliance weighting in defense.

alternatives.reading: One physical strength-2 alliance is two pieces in Mounting Defense.
alternatives.assessment: Not literal. It requires a weighted-strength substitution; no text says one alliance becomes multiple newly exhausted pieces.

alternatives.reading: The strength-2 alliance cannot defend a strength-1 Crisis because strength cannot be split.
alternatives.assessment: Rejected. The piece is exhausted once for a single defense purpose. No source requires all printed value to be matched or consumed exactly, and p33 can be satisfied by exhausting one physical piece.

alternatives.reading: Any printed excess is automatically fatal because p33 says do not equal.
alternatives.assessment: Rejected for stated case. That combines weighted value with a literal physical-count equality sentence without source authority. On the preferred reading the numbers are 1 and 1; on an ordinary weighted comparison the player-aid defender-wins-ties heading supports defense at least as strong as attack.

alternatives.reading: A scenario-specific FAQ is necessary before deciding strength 1.
alternatives.assessment: Rejected. The printed p33 piece count yields a direct result; the main coherent weighted alternative also favors defense against 1. Broader weighting uncertainty does not make this case unresolved.

quotes.quote: Local alliances are temporary Army pieces. Their strength can be used for two purposes: the Deploy action and to defend against threats in India during the Events in India phase. Each piece can only be used once on the turn they are purchased, and its strength cannot be split among more than one purpose.

Each officer or regiment you exhaust gives you one die. In addition, each local alliance in your Army you exhaust will give you the number of dice indicated on the piece. To exhaust an officer, regiment, or local alliance, move it to the bottom half of its respective Army box.

The Commander associated with the region must exhaust pieces in the Army equal to the strength of the Crisis or as many as possible. If the newly-exhausted pieces do not equal the strength of the Crisis, the Crisis succeeds. Perform the steps of Region Loss (page 29). If the attack failed, remove all unrest in the attacked region and the Commander associated with the region should take a trophy token.
Roll 1 die for each officer, regiment used. In addition roll dice equal to the strength of any alliances used.

quotes.note: Two distinct table column headers; punctuation semicolon added to separate the headers.

quotes.quote: Exhausted Regiments, Officers, and Local Alliances
quotes.note: Attack on the Company row, Defender Strength column. Unsuccessful attack column says Clear unrest. Commander gains a trophy.

quotes.quote: Any exhausted officers and regiments become active. Any active local alliances are exhausted.

Most actions that concern India require the acting player to make a check to see if their actions are successful. Each check requires a roll of the dice. The number of dice you roll is dependent on the resources you have and want to spend as determined by the action.
There are 20 regiments and 7 local alliance pieces which strengthen Company armies.

source_completeness_claim: Relevant authorized sections and the two full native aid pages were inspected. This is not a claim to have read the entire rulebook or every possible published clarification.
